Problems adapted from OpenStax University Physics Volume 1, ch. 13 Problems (Ling, Sanny, Moebs et al., 2016), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/1-introduction. Changes: given data stated inline, single-part. Answers computed from core/constants (answerExpr) and checked within tol. Hints: nudge (which idea), clue (formula; from the section's own worked examples, linked by 'learn'), walkthrough (numbers plugged in). Revealing the walkthrough means that question doesn't count toward the pass.

questions.q: Magnitude of the gravitational force between two 5-kg steel balls 15 cm apart (centre to centre)? (answer in N)
questions.explainer: Every two masses pull on each other: F = G·m₁·m₂ / r². Multiply the masses, divide by the distance squared, times G (6.674e-11). Calculator is fine.
hints: This is Newton's law of gravitation: two masses pulling on each other.
Every two masses pull on each other: F = G·m₁·m₂ / r². Multiply the masses, divide by the distance squared, times G (6.674e-11). Calculator is fine.
Plug the numbers in: G*5*5/0.15^2 (G = 6.674e-11, c = 3.00e8 m/s). Type that into a calculator.

questions.q: Escape speed from Mars (mass 6.418e23 kg, radius 3.38e6 m)? (answer in m/s)

hints: This is about energy and escaping a planet's pull.
Escape speed v = √(2·G·M / r). Potential energy between two masses U = −G·m₁·m₂ / r.
Plug the numbers in: √(2*G*6.418e23/3.38e6) (G = 6.674e-11, c = 3.00e8 m/s). Type that into a calculator.

questions.q: A planet with 1.5 times Earth's mass travels in Earth's orbit. Its period, in years? (answer in yr)
questions.explainer: For a circular orbit, T² = 4π²·r³ / (G·M). So you can weigh the thing being orbited from r and T: M = 4π²·r³ / (G·T²).
hints: This is about circular orbits: period, radius and the mass in the middle.

questions.q: Halley's comet: perihelion 0.586 AU, aphelion 17.8 AU, speed at perihelion 55 km/s. Speed at aphelion? (answer in km/s)
questions.explainer: Kepler: speed × distance is the same at perihelion and aphelion; period in years = (semi-major axis in AU)^1.5.
hints: This is Kepler's laws for elliptical orbits.
Kepler: speed × distance is the same at perihelion and aphelion; period in years = (semi-major axis in AU)^1.5.
Plug the numbers in: 55*0.586/17.8 (G = 6.674e-11, c = 3.00e8 m/s). Type that into a calculator.

questions.q: Schwarzschild radius of a black hole of 4 million solar masses (1 solar mass = 1.989e30 kg)? (answer in m)
questions.explainer: Schwarzschild radius r = 2·G·M / c²: squeeze a mass inside this and not even light escapes.
hints: This is about black holes and how small a mass must be squeezed.
Schwarzschild radius r = 2·G·M / c²: squeeze a mass inside this and not even light escapes.
Plug the numbers in: 2*G*4e6*1.989e30/c^2 (G = 6.674e-11, c = 3.00e8 m/s). Type that into a calculator.
